columns.label: Sim Variable
columns.help: The simulator's own name for this value: a SimConnect variable or event name, an FSUIPC hex offset, an X-Plane dataref path, a DCS-BIOS control id, a ProSim variable, a PSX Q-code, and so on. The Switch uses it to translate between the simulator and the Q-code. A row whose first cell starts with # is a comment and is ignored.

columns.label: SimStack Name
columns.help: A short friendly name for the value. The Loader uses it as the name in a sketch, so use letters, digits and _ only (no spaces). The Switch rejects a row whose name contains any of @ # $ % ^ * { } ( ) ~ ` ? , . / : " ; ' + - ! < > | \ and marks it ERROR.

columns.label: Q-code
columns.help: The SimStack code the boards use for this value: a prefix (Qs, Qh, Qi, Qe, Qa or Qc) followed by a number. It must start with a capital Q, must be unique in the file and must not contain spaces or punctuation. The prefix tells you the direction of the data (see the Q-code prefixes).

columns.label: Type
columns.help: The data type of the value. What is allowed depends on the simulator: for example FLOAT64 or INT32 for SimConnect and FSUIPC, float or command for X-Plane, integer, string or command for DCS. Some simulators (PSX, ProSim, JeeHell) do not use this column.

columns.label: Units
columns.help: Usually descriptive units such as Knots or Feet. For some rows it carries a number or an address instead: the string length for an FSUIPC or X-Plane STRING, the blob size in bytes for a PMDG ADDON parent, and the addr:mask:shift output spec for DCS.

columns.label: Resolution
columns.help: Controls when a change is sent. For most simulators it is epsilon:rateGroup — the smallest change worth sending, and how often it may be sent (0 = every frame, 1 = about 2 Hz, 2 = about 1 Hz, 3 = about every 5 s, 4 = once). The decimal point matters: 1 is rate group 1, but 1.0 is epsilon 1.0 with no rate cap. ADDON and BIT child rows put Qparent:offset here instead.

columns.label: Object
columns.help: The entry kind (also called encoding). USER is the normal value; ADDON marks a PMDG Client Data Area parent or child row. Most simulators ignore this column, and USER is the safe convention.

columns.label: Notes
columns.help: Free text for people. Use plain ASCII only. A comma inside the note must be in a quoted cell, or it starts a new column and shifts the formula.

columns.label: Evaluation
columns.help: Optional formula that the Switch runs on the value, in the form <S|C|B>;<TYPE>;arguments. S changes data from the simulator, C changes data from a board, B changes both. Leave empty for no change. Column 9 in the user guides (1-based) is this column.

Qs.label: Simulator variable
Qs.help: A value that comes from the simulator and goes to the boards (sim -> clients). PSX uses Qs for its system and background variables.

Qh.label: Event / hardware control
Qh.help: A control that a board sends to the simulator (clients -> sim), such as a switch, button or key event. SimConnect treats every Qh row as an event. PSX uses Qh for its human/hardware discretes.

Qi.label: Internal / interrogate
Qi.help: A value that can flow both ways. Also used for PMDG ADDON parent and child rows and for FSUIPC bit-field rows. PSX uses Qi for its commands.

Qe.label: Environmental
Qe.help: Environmental data such as power and temperature monitoring (sim -> clients).

Qc.label: Config
Qc.help: Configuration value internal to the Switch. It has no external simulator variable; with the Q Configuration licence the Switch stores the Resolution cell as the value.

epsilon_rate.help: Three forms are accepted. epsilon:rateGroup (for example 0.5:1) sets both. A number with a decimal point (for example 0.5) sets epsilon only, with no rate cap. A plain integer 0-4 (for example 2) sets the rate group only, with epsilon 0. Empty means epsilon 0, rate group 0. Use 0.0 as the epsilon for on/off and whole-number values. The epsilon must not be empty: ':1' is silently read as 0:0.

double.help: FlightGear reads this column as a plain number: the epsilon (smallest change worth sending). There are no rate groups. Empty means 0. Do not use the epsilon:group form — FlightGear cannot read it and uses 0.

addon_parent.help: PMDG ADDON parent row (Type BYTES): a rate group only, an integer 0-4. It sets how often the child fields are taken from the data blob. There is no epsilon. 2 (about 1 Hz) is a good default for cockpit panels.

addon_child.help: PMDG ADDON child row: the parent row's Q-code, a colon, then the byte offset of this field in the parent blob (a decimal integer from the addon SDK struct). The child uses the parent's rate group.

bit_child.help: FSUIPC BIT row: the parent row's Q-code, a colon, then one bit number or an inclusive range start-end. Bits are numbered 0-63 and end must not be less than start. Qi700:3 gives 0 or 1; Qi700:8-10 gives a 3-bit value 0-7.

simTypes.label: FSUIPC (MSFS/P3D/FSX via FSUIPC) and Sim-Avionics
simTypes.help: The Switch reads and writes FSUIPC memory offsets. Column 0 is the offset; the Type sets how many bytes are read. Sim-Avionics (simType 70) uses the same FSUIPC path and the same rules. Bit-field children (Type BIT) take single bits or bit ranges out of a parent offset row.

id.help: For a normal row, the FSUIPC offset in hex with a 0x prefix (or decimal). For a BIT child row, a unique field name (letters, digits, _) — it is not an offset.

type.help: The value type at the offset; it also sets the number of bytes read (INT8/BYTE 1, INT16/SHORT 2, INT32 4, INT64 8, FLOAT32 4, FLOAT64 8). STRING reads text. BIT marks a bit-field child row whose Resolution is Qparent:bit.

units.help: Descriptive units (Knots, Feet, Bool) or the legacy byte count (4, 8) — both work, because the byte size comes from the Type. For STRING, put the string length here (for example 256); if it is not a number the Switch uses 256.

resolution.help: epsilon:rateGroup, compared with the raw offset value before any formula. If airspeed is stored as knots x 128, an epsilon of 128.0 means 1 knot. A BIT child row puts Qparent:bit or Qparent:start-end here.

object.help: USER for a normal offset, CONTROL for a control offset you write to. The current FSUIPC code does not read this column, so it is a label only.

simTypes.label: SimConnect (MSFS/P3D) and PMDG addon data
simTypes.help: The Switch asks SimConnect for simulation variables by name, sends key events, and (with PMDG, simType 10) reads the addon's Client Data Area: one ADDON parent row (Type BYTES) defines the data blob and ADDON child rows pick fields out of it by byte offset. Every Qh row is sent as a key event.

id.help: The SimConnect variable or event name exactly as in the SDK, with an optional :index (GEAR POSITION:1) or an L: local variable (L:MyVar). For an ADDON parent, the CDA name from the addon SDK (PMDG_NG3_Data). For an ADDON child, any unique field name (MCP_Heading).

type.help: The SimConnect data type, in capitals (the Switch matches it exactly). FLOAT64 is the usual choice; STRING8...STRING260 or STRINGV for text. An ADDON parent is always BYTES. An ADDON child uses the C type of the field in the SDK struct: INT8, INT16, INT32, INT64, FLOAT32 or FLOAT64.

units.help: The SimConnect unit name (Knots, Feet, Degrees, Bool, Number) — SimConnect converts the value into this unit. For an ADDON parent, the blob size in bytes (for example 4096). For an ADDON child, descriptive only.

resolution.help: epsilon:rateGroup; SimConnect applies the epsilon itself, so small changes are never sent. An ADDON parent takes a rate group 0-4 only. An ADDON child takes Qparent:byteOffset, for example Qi499:268.

object.help: ADDON marks a PMDG Client Data Area parent or child row — the only value that changes behaviour. USER is a normal variable. EVENT/CONTROL label a key event (the Switch actually decides by the Qh prefix) and ONCE labels read-once data (use rate group 4 to read once).

simTypes.label: X-Plane (XPlaneConnect plugin or native UDP)
simTypes.help: The Switch reads and writes X-Plane datarefs and fires X-Plane commands. XPPLUGIN (21) uses the SimStack XPlaneConnect plugin; XPDIRECT (22) uses X-Plane's own RREF/DREF UDP protocol. The dictionary row is the same for both. A row is a command only when its Type is command.

id.help: The dataref or command path, for example sim/cockpit2/gauges/indicators/airspeed_kts_pilot. To read one element of an array, add the index at the end: instrument_brightness_ratio[1]. An un-indexed float array gives only element 0 on XPDIRECT.

type.help: float, int or double for a number (all arrive as float). command for an X-Plane command (send Qh=1 to execute, 2 to begin, 0 to end). byte[N] or STRING reads a byte array as text; int[N] reads it as a comma-separated list of N integers. float[N] is accepted but read as a plain number — index the dataref in column 0 instead.

units.help: Descriptive units (knots, degrees, ratio). For Type STRING, put the text length in bytes here (for example 40); a missing or bad length skips the row. Leave empty for command rows.

resolution.help: epsilon:rateGroup, applied by the Switch (XPDIRECT also uses the rate group to set the RREF rate). For byte arrays use a plain rate group such as 2. Leave empty for command rows.

object.help: Not read for X-Plane. USER is the convention; a command is marked in the Type column, not here.

simTypes.label: DCS World (via DCS-BIOS)
simTypes.help: The Switch reads DCS-BIOS's binary export and sends plain-text commands. DCS-BIOS must be installed in DCS. Column 4 carries the DCS-BIOS output address spec, not units. A row with sim in column 4 belongs to the SimStackControl.lua hook (pause, mission load).

id.help: The DCS-BIOS control identifier from the module JSON, used as-is in the command (UFC_1, AAP_PAGE). For a sim-control row, the hook value name (SIM_PAUSE).

type.help: integer (the default) reads (word & mask) >> shift; string reads len bytes from addr; command is send-only and has no readback.

units.help: The DCS-BIOS output spec: addr:mask:shift for an integer, addr:len for a string (hex with 0x, or decimal, from the module JSON address/mask/shift_by or max_length). Leave empty for a command row. Write sim for a sim-control hook row.

resolution.help: epsilon:rateGroup for integer outputs, for example 0:2. Strings are sent on change only, so a plain rate group is enough. Leave empty for command rows.

object.help: Not read for DCS. USER is the convention.

simTypes.label: FlightGear (Generic Protocol over UDP)
simTypes.help: The Switch builds a FlightGear Generic Protocol XML file from the dictionary; FlightGear then sends every property in one UDP line. After any dictionary change, press Connect, copy the XML to FlightGear's Protocol folder again and restart FlightGear.

id.help: The FlightGear property path, starting with /, for example /instrumentation/airspeed-indicator/indicated-speed-kt.

type.help: int, bool or string; anything else (or empty) is sent as float.

units.help: Descriptive units only (kts, deg, feet); not read by the Switch.

resolution.help: A plain number: the epsilon (smallest change worth sending). No rate groups and no colon.

object.help: Not read for FlightGear; may be empty.

simTypes.label: Aerowinx PSX
simTypes.help: PSX already speaks Q-codes, so the dictionary mainly gives each PSX variable its SimStack name for the Loader and carries optional formulas. Columns 3-6 are not used with PSX. PSX uses its own meanings for Qs (system), Qh (hardware discretes) and Qi (commands).

id.help: The PSX Q-code as listed in PSX's variables.txt (Developers folder), for example Qs1 or Qh28.

type.help: Not used with PSX (INT by convention).

units.help: Not used with PSX (1 by convention).

resolution.help: Not used with PSX — PSX sends changes as they happen (1 by convention).

object.help: Not used with PSX; leave empty.

simTypes.label: ProSim-AR (737 / A320)
simTypes.help: The Switch connects to ProSim over TCP and translates ProSim variable names to Q-codes with the dictionary. Columns 3-6 are not used. Rows whose name starts with S_ (switch) or CB_ (circuit breaker) get their values turned into ProSim state names (Normal/Pushed/Pulled).

id.help: The ProSim variable name exactly as ProSim uses it, for example S_MASTER_BATTERY_SWITCH.

type.help: Not used with ProSim; leave empty.

units.help: Not used with ProSim; leave empty.

resolution.help: Not used with ProSim — ProSim sends changes as they happen.

object.help: Not used with ProSim; leave empty.

simTypes.label: JeeHell FMGS A320
simTypes.help: The Switch connects to the SimStackJHA320.dll plug-in in JeeHell over TCP (port 10747). Column 0 is the JeeHell label in Tag:Index form. Columns 3-6 are not used but must be present.

id.help: The JeeHell label: S: switch input (to JeeHell), L: lamp/LED output, D: numeric data, T: text, followed by the index. Must match the JeeHell API exactly.

type.help: Not used with JeeHell (int by convention).

units.help: Not used with JeeHell (1 by convention).

resolution.help: Not used with JeeHell (1 by convention).

object.help: Not used with JeeHell. The samples label the tag kind: Switch, LED, Data or Text.

simTypes.label: Reentry (space capsule simulator)
simTypes.help: The Switch exchanges JSON messages with the Reentry game over UDP. Column 0 addresses one control as CRAFT:MSGTYPE:ID; values are whole-number positions.

id.help: TargetCraft:MessageType:ID, three whole numbers separated by colons, for example 0:0:3.

type.help: Not read; values are whole numbers (INT by convention).

object.help: Not read; the samples put the spacecraft name here (Mercury, Gemini, ApolloCommandModule).

simTypes.label: Other interfaces (API, DSix, MODBUS, UDP, NEW)
simTypes.help: Generic interfaces. API (3) behaves like PSX and passes Q-codes straight through. DSix (90) maps hex offsets such as 0x0001 in column 0 to Q-codes. UDP (99), MODBUS (91) and NEW (80) pass Q-codes with formulas. Only the general column rules apply.

formula.help: General form: <S|C|B>;<TYPE>;argument;argument... The Switch splits the cell at every ';' AND every '=' (so an '=' inside an expression or text breaks it into extra tokens). Empty tokens at the end are dropped, so a trailing ';' (S;DEFAULT;x/128;) is harmless. Do not put spaces in the direction or type token. Only the CONFIG type keeps its text whole.

directions.S: Server: change values that come from the simulator, before they go to the boards.
directions.C: Client: change values that come from a board or other client (also the web UI), before they go to the simulator.
directions.B: Both: change values whatever their origin.

expression.help: An exp4j expression where x is the incoming value. Use + - * / ^ (power) % (remainder), brackets, and the listed functions; trigonometry works in radians. Write multiplication explicitly (x*2). Example: (x-32)*5/9 converts Fahrenheit to Celsius.

functionHelp.ceil: Round up to a whole number: ceil(4.2) = 5
functionHelp.exp: e to the power x: exp(1) = 2.718
functionHelp.expm1: e to the power x, minus 1 (exact for small x)
functionHelp.floor: Round down to a whole number: floor(4.8) = 4
functionHelp.log1p: Natural logarithm of 1 + x (exact for small x)
functionHelp.pow: x to the power y: pow(2,3) = 8 (same as 2^3)

types.name: DEFAULT
types.help: Applies one formula to the value.

args.name: expression
args.help: The formula; x is the incoming value.

types.name: DEFAULT_BOUNDED
types.help: Applies one formula, then clamps the result between a lower and an upper limit.

args.name: expression
args.help: The formula; x is the incoming value.

types.name: MULTI
types.help: Applies several formulas to the same value and sends the results joined with ';'. Use it for example to turn a heading into sine and cosine.

args.name: expression
args.help: One formula per token; add as many as you need.

types.name: PLUSMINUS
types.help: Uses the first formula when the value is zero or positive, and the second when it is negative.

types.name: CONFIG
types.help: Ignores the incoming value and sends fixed configuration text instead.

args.name: data
args.help: Fixed text; any number of tokens.

types.name: LOOKUP
types.help: Reserved. The Switch recognises the name but does nothing — the value passes through unchanged. Do not use it.

types.name: SCRIPT
types.help: Calls a JavaScript function from the Switch's scripts folder (needs enableScripting=true in Switch.ini). Extra tokens are passed to the function as ctx.args. The name is case-sensitive.

args.name: function
args.help: The JavaScript function name, exactly as in the .js file.

args.name: arg
args.help: Optional extra arguments, passed as ctx.args.

types.name: CURVE
types.help: Maps the value through a response curve drawn on the Switch's Configuration > Curves tab (needs the Q Configuration licence; without it the value passes unchanged). Give the input and output ranges; the Switch warns when they are missing.

args.name: id
args.help: The curve profile number from the Curves tab.

args.name: centre
args.help: Optional, bipolar curves only: the raw input that means centre (default: midpoint of inMin..inMax).

types.name: VJOY
types.help: Sends the value to a vJoy virtual joystick axis or button, so the simulator sees the hardware as a game controller. The message then goes nowhere else: not to the simulator, not to the boards (before #780 it was also passed on). POV and SLIDER are accepted but do nothing yet.

args.name: index
args.help: Axis number (1 = X) or button number.

args.name: min
args.help: Input value for the axis minimum (min > max inverts the axis). For BUTTON, 1 inverts the button. If min or max is empty or not a number, the Switch uses 0 and 32768.

args.name: max
args.help: Input value for the axis maximum (empty = 32768, see min).

args.name: curve
args.help: Optional, AXIS only: a response curve id (needs the Q Configuration licence).

args.name: centre
args.help: Optional, bipolar curves only: the raw input that means centre.

types.name: CANBUS
types.help: Packs the value into a CAN bus signal and sends the frame on a named bus, with physical = raw x scale + offset. Do not put spaces around the tokens.

args.name: busId
args.help: The named CAN bus, for example overhead.

args.name: msgId
args.help: The CAN message id in hex, with or without 0x (1A0).

args.name: startBit
args.help: First bit of the signal (DBC convention).

args.name: bitLen
args.help: Number of bits in the signal.

types.name: ARINC740
types.help: Hands the value to the ARINC 740 cockpit printer handler.

types.name: ARINC739
types.help: ARINC 739 MCDU handler (parsed, but the processing is not active in the current Switch).

types.name: ARINC429
types.help: ARINC 429 data word handler (parsed, but the processing is not active in the current Switch; use SCRIPT with ARINCWord for 429 encoding).
